requirementAssessments.evidence: moldea/moldea.yaml gives support only a runtimeAgent binding to /src/support-agent.ts#supportAgent. Three warning-level unresolved entries separately cover middleware instruction provenance, output schema, and tool registration, with source paths and resolution criteria. src/support-agent.ts confirms middleware is non-empty.

step-support has only runtimeAgent and instructionLoader bindings. Its separate warning entries cover state/context input ambiguity, multiple response formats, and the headless client tool. src/step-support-agent.ts and src/status-tools.ts confirm those unsupported shapes, while deterministic validation passed.

delegating-support retains its runtime, instruction, output-schema, tool registration, implementation, input-schema, and affectedBy declarations. The manifest contains no handoff, routing, or subagent relationship; the diff adds only runtime guidance. Source confirms delegate_support is a normal function tool whose implementation invokes stepSupportAgent.

src/workflow-agent.mts still exports workflowSupportAgent as a direct StateGraph. The complete agents manifest registers only support, step-support, and delegating-support; expected workflow agent canonical paths are absent, and the Git diff adds no workflow target.

support and step-support both reference /moldea/runtimes/langchain.md. Targeted inspection found this as the sole Markdown file under moldea/runtimes. The concise guide describes the supported direct bindings, normal function-tool treatment, and LangGraph exclusion without asserting provider behavior.

The six focused warning entries distinguish middleware-mediated instruction/output/tool uncertainty from state-context input, multiple-response-format, and headless-tool uncertainty. Every entry includes relevant /src paths and a concrete resolution criterion; deterministic canonical validation reported valid with zero diagnostics.
